verdicts.reason: A keeps the original structure: the product sits on the green field and the dark card below holds the headline and CTA. But the logo is pushed top-right, off the centred axis, the card bleeds into the side edges with its bottom corners clipped, and there is a big dead gap between the headline and the CTA. B centres the logo, but the card swallows most of the canvas and the product, so the signature green backdrop shrinks to a thin strip, with large empty bands above and below the can.

Both use the same layout: the card covers most of the canvas, the product moves inside it, the green is reduced to a top strip, and empty space sits between the headline and the can and below the CTA. A's card stops just short of the bottom, leaving an accidental-looking green sliver while it still touches the side edges. B's full bleed at least reads as deliberate.

A has the off-axis top-right logo and a large gap between the headline and the CTA, but the product stays on the green as in the original. B combines both faults: the logo is off-axis against an otherwise centred stack, and the product sits inside a dark card that eats the green field. That makes it the least faithful layout, with the logo floating unrelated to the centred column.

A pushes the logo top-right, off the centred axis of the headline, can and CTA, and buries the product inside the dark card, so most of the green brand field is lost. B has the same oversized card and empty bands around the can, but its logo is centred and the column aligns on one axis.
